subject: Re: Term extension + capacity top-up — dedicated pool isolation plan and throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finlytics.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: dedicated capacity top-up & isolation questions

Hi Jonas —

We're coming up on our renewal and we're looking to increase committed capacity for our production cluster. A few items we need clarified before procurement signs off:

- Can Redwood reserve an isolated pool (logical separation) for FinLytics so no noisy neighbors affect our latency-sensitive jobs?
- If we increase to 40 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs, what's the throughput SLA you can offer and how is it measured?
- Any contract term or pricing changes tied to a larger committed reservation?

Attached is a draft SOW and a procurement redline; procurement looped in on CC.

Thanks —
Alyssa Chen
VP Product 
FinLytics
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, procurement@finlytics.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: dedicated capacity top-up & isolation questions

Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. Quick answers up front, then a proposed playbook so procurement has language they can use.

Summary: we can provision an isolated reserved pool for FinLytics with logical tenant fencing and a guaranteed throughput SLA tied to the committed GPU count. For 40 GPUs we recommend a 24-month term to keep unit pricing competitive; we also have a 12-month option with a smaller per-GPU discount.

Proposed next steps / what we need from you:
- Confirm target commit (40 GPUs) and preferred term (12 vs 24 mo).
- Sign off on isolation scope (logical fencing + dedicated QoS, see attached playbook).
- Procurement: agree on SLA measurement window (p95 token latency and tokens/s sustained over 30m windows).

Attached: FinLytics_SOW_draft.pdf, isolation_playbook_v1.xlsx

Neha (SE) — can you drop a short technical note here that describes how we'll implement the logical fencing and the expected throughput baseline for 40 GPUs? Include any caveats around quantized models and KV cache warmup.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0189
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finlytics.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-02T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Term extension + capacity top-up — isolation implementation notes

Alyssa / team —

Technical note from SE: we can implement the isolation you describe without physical node separation using the following components:

1) Reserved pool configuration: create a named reserved_pools entry for finlytics-prod that pins capacity (40 GPUs) to a set of instances with node affinity labels.

2) Logical fencing: request routing + namespace enforcement ensures only FinLytics tokens are routed to that pool. Tenant metadata and signing keys are validated at the edge; misrouted requests fail-fast (403).

3) QoS / throughput guarantees: we provide a baseline SLA of 9k-12k tokens/s (sustained) for the 40-GPU pool depending on model family and sequence length; contractual measurement will use sustained 30-minute windows and report p95 latency and aggregate tokens/s. We recommend specifying model families in the SOW (e.g., Llama-3 70B-8k vs. 33B) because throughput varies by architecture/quantization.

4) Cache & warmup caveats: when rolling to a new pool or after failover, KV-warmup can cause a transient drop in observed tokens/s. To mitigate, we suggest a 15-minute warmup window after cutover and an option for background prefix caching as part of the onboarding plan.

Sample config snippet for procurement / ops doc (non-exec):

reserved_pools:
  - name: finlytics-prod
    gpus: 40
    isolation: logical
    node_affinity: [gpu-type:a100, region:us-west-2]
    qos_profile: finlytics-sustained

qos_profiles:
  finlytics-sustained:
    target_tokens_per_second: 10000
    measurement_window_minutes: 30
    sla_metric: p95_latency_ms

I'll add these to isolation_playbook_v1.xlsx and flag the warmup section. Happy to jump on a 30-min tech deep-dive with your infra team if helpful.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Date: 2026-08-03T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Term extension + capacity top-up — PO redline and pricing question

Jonas —

Procurement here. The redline we attached asks for a 12-month term at the higher commit level and a 10% credit for the first month of onboarding to cover cutover risk (we'll run parallel jobs during the first 7–10 days). Can Redwood accommodate the 10% onboarding credit if we commit to 40 GPUs for 12 months?

Also need a clear definition of the SLA credit calculations (how do you calculate credits if tokens/s drops below target?).

Regards,
Marcus Doyle
Director, Procurement — FinLytics
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@finlytics.ai>, procurement@finlytics.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-03T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Term extension + capacity top-up — PO redline and pricing question

Marcus — appreciate the clear ask. Short answers:

- 12-month at 40 GPUs: we can accept the term but onboarding credit needs an approval signature from Ops/Revenue given it's outside standard SKUs. Vivek — can we approve a one-time 10% onboarding credit for FinLytics if they sign DL-FTX-2026-08 for 12 months at 40 GPUs?
- SLA credits: we calculate credits based on missed p95 latency targets over the contractual measurement windows. If sustained tokens/s falls below the target for X of the monthly windows, we prorate credits against monthly committed fees (detailed formula in SOW appendix). I'll include the exact formula in redline response.

If Ops approves the onboarding concession, we can route the updated PO back to you with the agreed credit line and the SOW language tightened around the SLA measurement.

Thanks —
Jonas
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Marcus Doyle <marcus.doyle@finlytics.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-04T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Term extension + capacity top-up — PO redline and pricing question

Jonas / Marcus —

Approve the one-time 10% onboarding credit for FinLytics subject to these two conditions:
1) FinLytics commits to the 12-month 40-GPU reservation (DL-FTX-2026-08) and signs the redlined SOW by EOD 2026-08-06.
2) We limit the credit to the first invoice only and exclude any credits triggered by customer misconfiguration during the onboarding window (per the warmup caveat Neha outlined).

Ops will coordinate with Billing to add the line item; Neha, please add the warmup exclusion language to the SOW appendix.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
